2. Corporate Theories

A firm can fund its business with debt or with equity. Does that choice change what the firm is worth? MM answers no, in a perfect market. With tax, the answer changes. This chapter starts at that benchmark and builds theories one at a time.

  • The MM Theorem: Does Capital Structure Change Value? — Suppose a firm earns 150 every year. It could be funded entirely with equity, or with a mix of debt and equity. Without tax, the two firms are worth the same. More debt does not move the value. The formula below is that claim. With tax, debt interest lowers the tax bill. Value rises by exactly that benefit. Move debt and watch the two lines pull apart. For example, imagine two friends opening identical snack bars. One funds it with her own money, the other borrows from a bank. Without tax, the two shops are worth the same: borrowed money does not make a shop more valuable. With tax, the borrower pays less tax thanks to interest, and the shop is worth more by that amount.
